newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha slips but U.S. propane, arb sets floor.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha slips but U.S. propane, arb sets floor.

text.p: NWE naphtha took one step back on Monday after several forward last week, and traders said firm U.S. propane prices and supplies that were drained from NWE should put a floor under prices.

"In total I think 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes moved last week to the States," a trader said. "For this week it would surprise me if we saw another move...I think the States has done what it is going to do for now."
Dec swaps fell $1 to $224.50/$225.50 with Jan holding at a $7.50 backwardation, at $217/$218. Feb fell about $3.50 to $209.50/$210.50.
NWE cargoes were notionally valued unchanged from Friday at $228/$230 cif.
He said traders were reluctant to sell naphtha with the crack spread so strong, near $50 a tonne, unless an armada of cargoes hits the Med or NWE, which was unlikely.
"I think last week it was the States (that supported NWE prices) and if that falls away we could be in for a small correction," he said, looking for only a minor pullback.
A broker said the cargoes may have moved to the U.S. to keep the pressure off NWE, since supplies were available here and buyers did not appear to be nervous.
"The market is so unpredictable...(but) I don't see the market coming off," he said.
The trader said a Skikda cargo and an Egyptian cargo were seen available in the first decade of December, but it was unclear whether they would go to the Med/NWE or U.S.
In NWE, two Russian cargoes out of Riga were coming to NWE this week, one at mid-week and another that will be loaded at mid-week and arrive at the weekend, he said.
The cargoes were seen between 5,000 and 10,000 tonnes.
A port official said on Monday Algeria's Skikda port may close later on Monday due to deteriorating weather.
He said oil loading berths were already out of action due to a heavy swell, but gas tankers were still able to load because they were more sheltered.
However, the weather forecast was for strengthening winds and rougher seas later on Monday, and he predicted all loadings would be suspended this afternoon.
